DescriptionOfMethod: Height of the main stem from the soil surface to the stem tip, measured with a ruler at the end of flowering, which is growth stage 69 on the BBCH scale. Five plants per plot are measured, taking every fifth plant along one of the middle rows and skipping the outer 0.5 m at each end of the plot. The score is the mean of the five plants, rounded to the nearest cm.

Colour of the flower petals, judged by eye on fully open flowers in the middle of flowering, for all plants in the plot or pot together. The codes are 1 for white petals with a dark spot on each wing petal, 2 for white petals with no spots, and 3 for purple or violet petals. When the plants differ, the colour of most of the plants is scored.

Absorbance of dried leaf powder, measured on a benchtop spectrometer that covers visible and near-infrared light from 400 to 2500 nm. Leaves from all plants in the plot or pot are dried at 60 degrees Celsius for 48 hours, ground to a fine powder and scanned in a sample cup. Each score is the absorbance at one wavelength, calculated as the base 10 logarithm of one divided by the reflectance. The wavelength is given as a feature.
